findings.location: docs/flows/download.batch.mmd: RETRY/CANCEL branches; docs/flows/contracts.md: 瀏覽器狀態
findings.consequence: The actual browser enables Cancel again after an uncertain submission result: download-batch.js finally sets batch-cancel.disabled=false even while pendingRequest remains. Clicking Cancel or pressing Escape closes the dialog and preserves selection, although the daemon may already have persisted tasks. The diagram has only RETRY → RPC and describes CANCEL as not sending tasks, omitting this reachable cancellation path and its existing-task consequence. Reopening also resets pendingRequest and generates a new request_id, so the previous identity is no longer available for retry.
findings.smallest_correction: Add RETRY → CANCEL and clarify the cancellation node/shared contract: closing sends no further request and preserves selection, but does not undo a submission whose result is unknown; reopening generates a new request identity.

limitations: Read-only source and recorded-test-evidence review; no application code or tests executed by this reviewer.
Existing browser tests exercise lost-response retry and cancellation separately, but do not exercise cancellation after an uncertain response.
Rust end-to-end forwarding, real NAS, external services, production environment and diagram rendering remain unverified as recorded in supplied evidence.
Index coverage for relied-on application and test paths reported no_recorded_issue / metadata_match; this is best-effort metadata, not proof of semantic completeness.
